bos_q3_2026.title: Business Outlook Survey—Third Quarter of 2026
bos_q3_2026.field_dates: In-person/video/phone interviews Aug 6–Sep 2, 2026; about three-quarters preceded the Aug 21 Canada–US trade-talk breakdown and counter-tariffs.
bos_q3_2026.population_and_limit: About 100 senior managers of firms selected to reflect business-sector GDP; report cautions small sample limits statistical reliability.
reported_facts: Sentiment improved from Q2; past and expected sales strengthened, with future-sales balance above historical average. Export outlooks remained above average, attributed to solid US demand and high oil prices.
Investment intentions eased slightly but remained robust. Hiring intentions stayed soft/below historical average; most firms expected unchanged headcount.

Most firms reported spare capacity. The share with difficulty meeting unexpected demand rose to historical average, though few expected significant difficulty. Binding labour shortages were roughly unchanged and below historical levels.
Input/selling-price growth and firms’ inflation expectations eased overall but remained elevated; firms with unusually large cost increases planned more pass-through.

Responses collected after Aug 21 showed weaker sentiment/export outlooks and higher inflation expectations. This was the minority post-breakdown sample; the report cautions sample composition may explain some differences.

csce_q3_2026.title: Canadian Survey of Consumer Expectations—Third Quarter of 2026
csce_q3_2026.field_dates: Online panel Aug 5–27; 77% collected on/before Aug 21, 23% afterward; follow-up calls Aug 24–Sep 4.
csce_q3_2026.series_source: Official CSCE Chart 1 CSV, linked from the report; series definitions identify current perceptions and 1-, 2-, and 5-year-ahead inflation expectations. Values are percent.
csce_q3_2026.other_reported_facts: Report: 12-/24-month expectations little changed, 5-year rose to meet shorter horizons; all horizons higher post-Aug 21, with sample-composition caveat. Labour perceptions improved slightly but stayed below survey average; spending intentions weakened.

mps_q2_2026_context_only.timing_limit: June survey/July release precedes Aug–Oct survey and CPI evidence; does not incorporate later observations.

limits: Surveys are respondents’ views, not outcomes or an October decision signal by themselves.
BOS small/interview-based; CSCE post-event comparisons may reflect sample composition.
